Q: How to call a function from a Button in Swift A:

Note that in your sample code, you use the selector name buttonTap in your call to addTarget:action:for: and then your IBAction method is called tapButton. Also you need the @objc tag on the method that you are going to use for the target/action.

Q: Segfault when running function in heap with executable permissions A:

The instruction e8 c5 fe ff ff decoded as call 1080 <putchar@plt> is a bit misleading.

According to the documentation, the mnemonic for e8 is "CALL rel32" and the description is "Call near, relative, displacement relative to next instruction". And you should have been able to tell that there is something fishy here, because the operand 0xfffffec5 is not 1080; it is -315.

So, this instruction is not really a call 1080; it is a call -315, and it just so happened that the next instruction in the original function was located at such an address that by subtracting 315 from it, the CPU landed at 1080, which is where putchar@plt happens to be located in memory.

By copying this function but leaving the operand the same, you are instructing the CPU to jump at an offset of -315 bytes from the new position of the function; this is not address 1080 anymore; it is something random, which results in the SegFault you are experiencing.

So, if you want to copy this function, you need to either replace the call instruction with another one that accepts an absolute operand, or you need to do the necessary math (it is just an addition and a subtraction) to compute the right relative offset to arrive at location 1080 from a different location in memory.

Q: General advice about pursuing a career in computer programming A:

I find Python to be far simpler than C and C++ (which require knowledge of memory usage and pointers), or C# and Java (which require knowledge of object-oriented concepts). I too learned Basic first, then Pascal, but they are not practical options anymore. In my view, Python is the new Basic.
